questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to trace your family history on a TV programme
Why people in Britain should pay more taxes
The census: what it is, why it began and how it changed
The history of the Roman army and its soldiers
questions.why: They discuss what a census is for, why it was created and how counting people changed over time.

questions.q: How often has Britain carried out a census since 1801?
options: Every year
Every five years
Every hundred years
Every ten years
questions.why: Sam says a census has been carried out every ten years since 1801.

questions.q: What happened in 2002 when old census records went online?
options: So many people visited that the website crashed
Very few people were interested in looking at them
The government removed them again after a few days
People found many serious mistakes in the records
questions.why: So many people rushed to access them that the website crashed.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention the story of Mary and Joseph travelling to Bethlehem?
options: To explain where the word 'census' comes from
To show that censuses have a very long history
To show that censuses were religious events
To compare Roman and British governments
questions.why: He says other censuses have a much longer history, and this story is linked to a Roman census.

questions.q: According to Dr Kathrin Levitan, what were the two main reasons for early censuses?
options: Building new roads and schools in the countryside
Counting the number of children and old people
Finding soldiers for wars and collecting taxes
Planning new cities and hospitals for the poor
questions.why: She says censuses were used to find who could fight in wars and for purposes of taxation.

questions.q: How were early censuses usually carried out?
options: Officials went from house to house asking questions
People filled in forms at the post office
Soldiers counted people in the streets
Churches kept lists of everyone
questions.why: Sam says they often involved officials going from house to house asking about the people there.

questions.q: According to Andrew Whitby, what was new about the 1890 US census?
options: It was the first census to count women
It was done completely by clerks by hand
It was the first to be done online
Punched cards were read by a machine
questions.why: He says each record was punched onto a card and the cards were fed through a machine.

questions.q: Why have some people questioned the need for a census today?
options: Because it is far too expensive to organise
So much personal data is already online
Because people refuse to answer
Because populations don't change much
questions.why: Sam says so much personal information is freely available online that some question the need for a census.
